about: Cases for Layer B. `expect` is what the check must never violate: NOT_SUPPORTED means the answer must not be SUPPORTED (UNCLEAR or CONTRADICTED are both fine); MAY_SUPPORT means the claim is true, SUPPORTED is welcome, UNCLEAR is acceptable, CONTRADICTED would be a false alarm. `gold` is a passage from the source, read by a person this week, that a reader would need to see; retrieval is judged on whether it reaches the model. `origin`: real = the sentence and the error both existed in this project; reconstructed = real source and error, sentence rewritten; injected = real source, error added for the test.

cases.sentence: Kurtić et al. report that all quantization schemes recover over 99% of the average score on the OpenLLM Leaderboard v1.
Gupta and MacAvaney show that annotators could not find answers to 38-45% of MS MARCO queries, which were then discarded.
GPTQ quantizes the weights of very large language models to 3 or 4 bits per weight.
Kurtić et al. report over 500,000 evaluations of quantized Llama-3.1 models, finding recovery above 99% for every scheme tested.
Survivorship bias has been formalised in the MS MARCO benchmark by Gupta and MacAvaney.
Vovk introduced Mondrian conformal predictors in his paper on the conditional validity of inductive conformal predictors.
Their score matrix covers 84 frontier models and 233 benchmarks and is approximately rank-2.
Quantized checkpoints do not appear in the BenchPress paper.
